title: Cumulative Review 1: Modules 1 to 3
intro: Spaced review mixes questions from earlier modules. Retrieving older material now is what makes it stick. Items you miss come back for a retry round.

items.q: Which measure of variability depends only on two scores?
items.why: The range uses only the highest and lowest scores, which makes it sensitive to outliers.

o: The most frequently occurring score or category
items.why: The mode is the only measure of central tendency that works for nominal data.

o: Averages out to the population value across many samples
Is computed from the whole population
items.why: Unbiased does not mean any single estimate is correct. It means the long run average is right.

items.q: Temperature in degrees Fahrenheit is measured on which scale?
items.why: Equal intervals but no true zero. Zero degrees Fahrenheit does not mean no temperature, so 80 is not twice as hot as 40.

o: A score divided by the mean
The square root of the variance
The difference between the highest and lowest scores
items.why: X minus the mean. Deviations from the mean always sum to zero.

items.q: The sum of products (SP) in the correlation formula
o: Adds up, for each person, the X deviation times the Y deviation
Is the sum of squared X deviations
items.why: SP captures how X and Y deviate together. Positive products dominate when high X goes with high Y.

items.q: The sum of squared deviations from the mean is abbreviated
items.why: SS stands for sum of squares. It is the starting point for variance and standard deviation.

items.q: The difference between a sample statistic and the population parameter it estimates is
items.why: Sampling error is the natural discrepancy that arises because a sample is only part of the population.

items.q: Degrees of freedom for a single sample variance equal
items.why: Once the sample mean is fixed, only n minus 1 scores are free to vary.

items.q: Which design includes random assignment of participants to conditions?
items.why: Random assignment is what defines a true experiment and is what supports cause and effect claims.

items.q: Reaction time in milliseconds is measured on which scale?
items.why: Zero means no time, and ratios make sense. 600 ms is twice as long as 300 ms.
Strength depends on the absolute value, not the sign.
